strategies.name: Baseline 8-stage sequential all-reduce
strategies.desc: Directly follows the reference: 8 sequential all-reduce operations with interleaved bidiagonal coupling/decoupling local ops. 8 collective dispatches total (one all-reduce per stage). Represents the straightforward interpretation with no fusion or overlap, serving as the performance baseline.

strategies.name: Fused bidiagonal kernel per stage
strategies.desc: Fuse the coupling and decoupling local operations into single vectorized kernels executed between all-reduces, eliminating intermediate buffer writes. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces memory traffic and kernel launch overhead by combining the forward coupling, backward decoupling, and division operations into monolithic compute passes.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter then all-gather per stage
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather (16 dispatches total). Each rank only computes its owned shard's bidiagonal coupling locally between RS and AG, requiring point-to-point communication or halo exchange for boundary terms (shard r+1 data). Trades more dispatches for potentially better network utilization on large world sizes.

strategies.name: Pipelined multi-stage with async dispatch
strategies.desc: Issue all 8 all-reduce operations asynchronously with xm non-blocking semantics, interleaving local computation (coupling/decoupling) as soon as each stage's result arrives. Approximately 8 dispatches but overlaps communication with computation across stages. Requires careful dependency tracking to respect stage ordering while maximizing pipeline fill.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction with node-local aggregation
strategies.desc:
Exploit 224 = 28 nodes × 8 devices structure by performing intra-node all-reduce first (8-way), then inter-node all-reduce (28-way), then intra-node broadcast for each of the 8 stages. Approximately 24 dispatches (3 collectives × 8 stages) but reduces cross-node bandwidth pressure by aggregating within NUMA domains first.
